assertions.name: both published figures are the correct roundings of the bare-form inversion at their CODATA vintage — the numbers were right, only unwitnessed
but it is FIVE orders below the quoted uncertainty, not six — the block said six and is corrected

description: Triages the two q-from-alpha_EM figures in tbl:substrate-consistency-window-table1-data, flagged by the unsourced-published-figures sweep as having no producer anywhere in the repo (every alpha_EM inversion module is deprecated, and the block's .ts cites nothing computational). Inverting the bare form alpha^-1 = q [9]_q [10]_q at 40 dps: CODATA 2018 (137.035999084) gives q = 1.11023043770666 and CODATA 2022 (137.035999177) gives q = 1.11023043781657, whose roundings are exactly the published 1.11023043771 and 1.11023043782. The quoted 1.1e-10 shift is also correct (measured 1.0991e-10). One overstatement corrected: that shift is FIVE orders below the quoted +-0.00002, not six. Verdict: correct but unwitnessed; the fix is to record the producer, not to change the numbers. These are NOT q0 -- they are the electromagnetic determination of q, and the bare form gives ~136.82 at q0, the gap being the Chern-Simons dressing.
caveats: Says nothing about whether the bare form is the right model of alpha_EM; that is rem:em-coupling-chern-simons and rem:alpha-em-derivation-open-problems, explicitly open.
These q values are NOT the substrate anchor q0 and are not meant to equal it. The block does not claim they do.
